_readme: EVENTS V2: three complete arcs in the proposed v2 format (design.md, part 2). Design sample, not loaded by the game. Every event here is a v1 LifeEvent plus the optional v2 fields: entry, talk (nodes, replies, ends), activity, promise, debt, objective, arc, nemesis. Text was written to the de-ai skill (zocial-gen-operations/.claude/skills/de-ai) and run through its detector. Checked by work/check.py: every goto, result and end resolves; reply labels are 72 characters or under; spoken lines 240 or under.

arcs.title: A hundred balls in the dark
arcs.summary: The kit man offers to feed you a hundred balls after a bad game. Say yes and you play the drill. He tells the manager, the drill becomes a thing the two of you do, your best score goes on the kit room door, and seasons later he retires and holds you to a promise.

beats.title: A hundred balls in the dark

event.title: A hundred balls in the dark
event.speaker: kitman

entry.hint: He has a bag of balls and nowhere to be

setup: Training finished forty minutes ago. {kitman.name} is still on pitch two with a bag of balls, and the only light is the one over the mower shed.

say: "You were snatching at them Saturday. I've a bag of balls here and the groundsman's left the shed light on, so do you want me to feed you a hundred?"

replies.label: "Go on then, feed me a hundred."
"Was I that bad?"
"Not tonight, {kitman.short}, I'm done in."
Say nothing.

say: "You put three over the bar and you looked at the keeper before every one of them."
"I've washed the kit here for thirty-one years and I've seen a lot of lads go through that. Most of them got out of it on a night like this."

replies.label: "So what do I do about it?"
"You wash the kit, {kitman.short}."
"I hear you, but not tonight."

say: He waits a bit, then tips the bag out. "You don't have to say owt. Stand on the D and I'll roll them in."

replies.label: Walk to the D.
Shake your head and go in.

say: "I do. And your boots will be clean on your peg by eight tomorrow, same as they always are." He starts putting the balls back in the bag.

replies.label: "That came out wrong and I'm sorry. Can I still have the hundred?"
Leave him to it.

say: "Fair enough, you've trained all day. I'm out here most Thursdays if you change your mind."

replies.label: "I'll come out Thursday, and I mean that."
"See you tomorrow."

say: {if said:snapped}"Right." He doesn't look up. {/if}"Ten lots of ten, and I count them out loud so neither of us can cheat."
"Do you want them from where you missed on Saturday, or from further out where it's harder?"

replies.label: "From where I missed, low in the corners."
"Further out, from twenty yards."
"You've watched more of this than me. You pick."

say: "Corners, then. Twenty yards is for when you can do the corners."

replies.label: "Corners."

say: "One more thing before we start. The gaffer's going to see that light from his office window. If he asks me in the morning, what am I telling him?"

replies.label: "Tell him it was me."
"Nothing. This stays on pitch two."
"Tell him you made me do it."

activity.name: Den's hundred
activity.intro: Ten balls. Each one stands for ten. He rolls them in from your left and counts.
activity.score: balls that finish inside a marked corner (0-10); shown as tens

lines: "Seventy, and stop looking at the goal."

say: "{activity.tens} out of a hundred. I'll be honest with you, I had you down for fifty."

replies.label: "Same again Thursday?"
"I needed that, {kitman.short}, thanks."

say: "{activity.tens}. That's {activity.tens} more than you hit on Saturday, and the last two lots were the best you struck all night."

replies.label: "I want another go at it. Thursday?"
"Thanks for staying out."

say: "{activity.tens}. It's dark, mind, and my feeding's not what it was. You were still looking up before you hit it."

replies.label: "Then I'm back Thursday until I stop doing it."
"I can't see the ball out here."

say: "That's {activity.tens}, and we said a hundred." He looks at the balls still in the bag, then at you.

replies.label: "I'm sorry, but my legs have gone."
"That'll do me."

say: "I've a flask of soup in the van if you want a cup before you go. It's only tomato."

replies.label: "Go on, and I'll carry the bag."
"Thanks, but I'd better get off."

say: You sit on the back step of the van. {if legend}"I did this with {legend.name} when he was nineteen, and he'd not thank me for telling you he was worse at it than you."{/if}

"I've two more seasons in me. The wife says one. When I do go they'll give me a night, a dinner or a match or something, and I'd like you there. Lads always say yes and then they've signed for somebody in Spain."

replies.label: "I'll be there, wherever I'm playing by then."
"If I can get there, I will."
"You'll still be here when I've retired."

ignored.text: You go in with the others. From the car park you can see him kicking the balls back into the bag one at a time.

snubbed.text: He zips the bag and carries it in on his own. In the morning your boots are clean on your peg, and he doesn't say good morning.

left.text: "See you tomorrow." He turns the shed light off himself.

thursday.text: "Thursday." He writes it on the back of his hand in biro, which is where he writes everything.

broken.text: Thursday came and you went home. He waited until half six.

walked-off-honest.text: "Then go and put them in the ice. We'll finish it another night." He means it.

walked-off.text: He collects the rest himself. It takes him a while, because some of them went a long way wide.

stayed.text: It's gone seven when you get to your car. Your right foot aches in a way you quite like.

stayed-promised.text: "I'll hold you to that." He pours the soup into the flask lid and gives you the lid.

promise.text: Be at {kitman.short}'s night when he retires

stayed-maybe.text: "That's all anybody can say." The soup is too hot and you both drink it anyway.

stayed-joked.text: He laughs, and then he tells you about the 1998 cup run, twice.

callbacks.line: "Pitch two's free Thursday, if your legs are up to it."
Your boots are on your peg, clean. He has left the laces out.

event.title: The light over the mower shed
event.speaker: manager
setup: {if arc.tell==1}{manager.name} stops you outside the boot room. {kitman.short} is in there with the door open, pairing socks.{/if}
{if arc.tell==0}{manager.name} stops you outside the boot room. "Somebody had the shed light on till seven last night. {kitman.short} says he can't think who."{/if}

say: {if arc.tell==1 && arc.last>=50}"{kitman.short} tells me you were out on pitch two till gone seven, and that you hit {arc.last} out of a hundred."{/if}
{if arc.tell==1 && arc.last<50}"{kitman.short} tells me you were out on pitch two last night. He also tells me you stopped at {arc.last}."{/if}
{if arc.tell==0}"Was it you?"{/if}

replies.label: "I needed it after Saturday, gaffer."
"It was me. I'm working on my finishing."
"Yes. So start me Saturday and you'll see it."
"Not me, gaffer."
No comment.

say: "Hm." He looks at your boots, which have fresh grass on them, and then walks on.

replies.label: Go and get changed.

say: "What did he have you doing?"

replies.label: "Low in the corners. I keep looking at the keeper."
"Bit of shooting."

say: {if talk.mood>=1}"He's right about the keeper. I've had the video lads clip it for you and it's on the laptop in my office when you want it."{/if}
"On Saturday, when you get your chance, I want it low and I don't want to see you look up. Can you do that for me?"

replies.label: "Low, and I won't look up."
"If I score like that, I'm on the penalties."

denied.text: In the boot room {kitman.short} says nothing, and pairs the same two socks again.

objective.text: "Good lad." Behind him {kitman.short} gives you a thumbs up with a sock on it.
"And next time, finish the hundred." He says it loud enough for the boot room to hear.

objective-bet.text: He nearly smiles. "Score like that and we'll talk about the penalties."

callbacks.line: "You still want those penalties?"

event.title: A note in your left boot
event.speaker: kitman
setup: When the ball went in you looked at the tunnel, and {kitman.short} had both hands up with all ten fingers out.
After the game there's a note folded in your left boot. "Corners. Thursday?" He's signed it, in case you thought it was from somebody else.

choices.label: Put the note in your washbag.

outcomes.text: It's still in there at the end of the season, gone soft at the folds.
"Next one's yours. Miss it and it goes back."
He finds it when he cleans them, and that's the last note you get from him.

callbacks.line: "He's still got a note I left in his boot. I've seen it in his washbag."

event.title: Thursdays on pitch two
event.speaker: kitman
setup: Thursday, and the bag is already out on pitch two.

say: {if arc.path=='snubbed'}He sees you coming and keeps counting the balls into the bag. "Did you want something?"{/if}
{if arc.path=='left'}"You came, then. I'd half put the bag away."{/if}
{if arc.path=='stayed' && arc.nights<3}"Your best is {arc.best}. From the same place, or are we moving you back?"{/if}
{if arc.path=='stayed' && arc.nights>=3}"{arc.best} to beat. I've started bringing two flasks, by the way, because you drink all the soup."{/if}

replies.label: "Same place, because I want {arc.best} beaten."
"Move me back to twenty yards."
"Is the offer still there? The hundred?"
"I was out of order the other night."
"Can we just have the soup tonight?"
Say nothing.

say: He rolls one out to you anyway.

replies.label: Hit it.
Roll it back and go in.

say: "You were. I've had worse off better players, mind." He tips the bag out again. "Go and stand on the D."

replies.label: Stand on the D.

say: "Aye, go on." You sit on the van step.
"My grandson's started at the under-nines. He's a left back and he hates it, he wants to be you. I told him you'd been doing corners for a month and he said that sounded boring."

replies.label: "Bring him one Thursday and I'll feed him some."
"He's right, it is boring."

say: "{activity.tens}. That's the most you've hit out here." He writes it on the back of his hand.

replies.label: "Don't wash that hand."
Help him pick the balls up.

say: "{activity.tens} tonight. {arc.best} is still the one to beat."

replies.label: "Can I come back next Thursday?"

say: "Stopping there? Suit yourself, there's a game Saturday."

replies.label: "Saving my legs."

not-tonight.text: He catches it under his foot and watches you go.

soup.text: You sit there until the shed light goes off on its timer.

soup-grandson.text: "He'll be sick with nerves. I'll bring him."

promise.text: Feed {kitman.short}'s grandson some balls one Thursday

kept.text: The lad hits four out of ten and tells everyone at school it was nine.

broken.text: The lad came three Thursdays running in his boots. You weren't there for any of them.

new-best.text: In the morning your number is chalked on the inside of the kit room door, with {activity.tens} next to it.

new-best-helped.text: Some of them have gone as far as pitch three. In the morning your number is chalked inside the kit room door, with {activity.tens} next to it.

night.text: You have a cup of soup on the van step and then you drive home.

stopped.text: He doesn't mind. He counts what's left back into the bag.

callbacks.line: "The little one's stopped asking about you, if you were wondering."

event.title: The kit room door
event.speaker: kitman
setup: {kitman.short} opens the kit room door all the way so you can see the back of it. There are forty years of chalk on it, numbers and scores in different handwriting.
Near the top it says 94, with the number nine beside it and the year 2009.

say: "That's {if legend}{legend.name}'s{/if}{if !legend}the old number nine's{/if}. Nobody's got near it since. You're on {arc.best}, and I've only one piece of chalk left, so I'm not writing you up there for a ninety-three."

replies.label: "Get the bag and I'll do it tonight."
"How many goes did it take him?"
"Leave his up there, it's his door."

say: "All of one winter. He did it the week after his dad's funeral and he never came out again after, he said he'd done it."

replies.label: "Get the bag."
"Then it stays his."

activity.name: The door
activity.intro: Ten balls from twenty yards. Ten out of ten beats the door.

say: He doesn't say anything for a bit. Then he goes in and gets the chalk.

replies.label: "Put me underneath his."
"A hundred goes at the top."

say: "{activity.tens}. He missed it plenty of times as well, I'll tell you that for nothing."

replies.label: "Keep the chalk somewhere safe."

left-it.text: "He'd like that." He shuts the door. {if legend}He'll tell {legend.short}, as well, you can see him deciding to.{/if}

on-the-door-under.text: Your number goes on the door under his, with 100 beside it and this year. His hand shakes a bit doing the zeros.

on-the-door-top.text: He has to stand on a crate to reach. Your number goes above the 94. Somebody will tell the old number nine by lunchtime.

short.text: The chalk goes back in his top pocket. This beat comes round again the next time you beat your best.

callbacks.line: "I hear I've been moved down a door."
"Had a young lad in the kit room yesterday asking whose hundred that was."

event.title: "I'm finishing in May"
event.speaker: kitman

variants.setupSwap: It's the old club's landline. You know the number because it has never changed.

setup: {kitman.short} is labelling next season's pegs, and he has stopped at his own coat hook.

say: "I've told the gaffer and I've told the chairman, so I'm telling you. I'm finishing in May. The wife was right about the knees."
{if promise(p-dens-night)}"They're giving me a night at the ground, the last Friday of the season. You said you'd come, on the van step, and I wrote it down."{/if}
{if !promise(p-dens-night)}"They're giving me a night at the ground, the last Friday of the season. I'd like you there, if you're about."{/if}

replies.label: "I said I'd be there. I'll be there."
"The last Friday? I'll be there."
"The last week's tight, {kitman.short}. I'll try."
Say nothing.

say: "I know it is. I've done the last week of the season thirty-odd times." He goes back to the pegs.

replies.label: "No. Put my name down. I'm coming."
Leave it there.

say: "Good. There's one more thing and you can say no. They want somebody to stand up and say a few words, and the chairman asked who. I said you."

replies.label: "I'll do it. I'm not good at it, but I'll do it."
"I'll come, but somebody else should talk."
"Why me? You've had better players than me."

say: "I have. But they went in when training finished."

replies.label: "All right. I'll say a few words."
"I'll be there. I can't do a speech."

hedged.text: He writes the last peg label and sticks it on crooked.

coming.text: "That'll do me." It goes on the back of his hand.

speech.text: "Keep it short. And don't tell them about the soup, they'll all want some."

promise.text: Say a few words at {kitman.short}'s night

event.title: The last Friday of the season
event.speaker: kitman

entry.text: "Friday. 7 o'clock at the ground. Wear a shirt with a collar. D"

clash.line: It is the same night as a sponsor dinner at your new club.

setup: There are four hundred people on the pitch at round tables, and a small stage where the centre circle is. {kitman.short} is in a suit. Nobody here has seen him in one before.
{if mem(kitman,'you-went-to-the-ward')}Two nurses from the children's ward are on his table.{/if}

say: {manager.name} taps the microphone. "He asked for one of the players to say something, and he picked this one." He hands it to you.

replies.label: Tell them about pitch two, and the shed light.
Thank him, plainly, for thirty-odd years of clean boots.
Tell them your score on the door, and who counted it.
Tell them the club never paid him enough.
No comment.

say: You stand there with the microphone and nothing comes. {kitman.short} shouts from his table: "He's better with a ball. Somebody give him a ball." People laugh, and it lets you off.

replies.label: "What he said, and thanks, {kitman.short}."

say: {if said:had-a-go-at-the-club}The chairman's table has gone quiet, and the tables at the back are clapping. {kitman.short} is looking at his plate, but he's smiling.{/if}
{if !said:had-a-go-at-the-club}It lasts about a minute. When you get to the soup, he shouts "I told you not to mention the soup," and four hundred people laugh.{/if}

replies.label: Sit down next to him.

say: "They want a bit of a show before the raffle. There's a goal up at the far end. Crossbar, you against {if legend}{legend.short}{/if}{if !legend}the gaffer{/if}, five each, and the tables are putting money on it for the children's ward."
"I'll count."

replies.label: "Go on. A week of my wages says I win."
"I'll play. Keep my money out of it."
"Not in these shoes. Let the kids have a go."

say: "{activity.score} to {activity.oppScore}. The ward gets the lot either way, so don't look so pleased."

replies.label: "Double it. Put mine in as well."
Take the applause.

say: "{activity.oppScore} to {activity.score}, to the old man. I've watched you hit that bar for fun on a Thursday."

replies.label: Pay up and shake his hand.

say: It's late. The tables are being stacked, and he has walked you out to the car park to the van.
"I'm not allowed to take anything that belongs to the club. But the bag's mine, I bought it in 1994." He gets the ball bag out of the back. "There's forty in there. Some of them are older than you."

replies.label: "I'll look after it."
"Leave it for the next kit man. I'll tell him why."
"Only if you come and feed me on Thursdays."

took-the-bag.text: It goes in your boot. It smells of grass and dubbin, and it will be in your garden from tomorrow.

took-the-bag-thursdays.text: "I'll bring the soup." He does, most Thursdays, to your garden, until his knees stop him driving.

bag-stays.text: He puts it back in the kit room himself, on the hook where it has always been. The new man starts in July.

@send-apologies.text: You send a signed shirt and a card. He props the card against the water jug on his table. The chair with your name on it stays empty, and it is in the back of most of the photos.

@ignore.text: You don't answer, and the Friday goes by. On Saturday the club posts the photos. There's a chair with your name card on it and nobody in it.

callbacks.line: "Busy Friday, was it? There was a chair free."
{kitman.short} is first on your own guest list, and he has already rung to ask about parking.

event.title: A letter in his handwriting
event.speaker: kitman
setup: A real letter, with a stamp on it. The envelope has your squad number where the house number should be, and it got here anyway.
"No hard feelings, I know how the last week goes. They gave me a clock and a lawnmower. I'm out the back most afternoons and the bag is in my shed if you're ever passing. The soup offer stands. D"

outcomes.text: He's on his knees in a flower bed when you pull up. He makes you carry the mower back to the shed before he'll put the kettle on.
It takes you three goes. He writes back inside a week, two sides, mostly about the lawn.
It's still in the drawer when you move house.

callbacks.line: Going through the guest list, you get to the staff and stop at the kit man's line.

event.title: Somebody else's bad Saturday
event.speaker: kid

entry.hint: He missed two on Saturday and he's still out here

setup: Training finished forty minutes ago and {kid.name} is still on pitch two, on his own, hitting balls at an empty goal and going to fetch every one.
{if arc.bag==1}{kitman.short}'s old bag is in the boot of your car.{/if}

say: He stops when he sees you. "Sorry. I'll get out of the way, I was only going to do a few more."

replies.label: "Stand on the D. I'll roll you a hundred."
"You're looking at the keeper. I used to do it."
"Don't stay out too long."

say: "A hundred? Have you not got somewhere to be?"

replies.label: "Not tonight, so it's ten lots of ten and I count."
"A kit man did this for me. I owe somebody one."

activity.name: You feed, he shoots
activity.intro: Roll ten passes onto his right foot. A good feed gives him a better chance.
activity.score: his corners out of 10, helped by how many of your passes went through the gate

say: "{activity.tens}! Did you see the last one?" He's out of breath and he can't stop grinning.

replies.label: "Same time Thursday, and bring a coat."
"That's how you hit it Saturday."

say: "{activity.tens}. That's rubbish, isn't it."

replies.label: "I got forty my first night. Thursday?"
"It's not good, so come back Thursday."

say: "Oh. Right. Thanks for the ones you did."

replies.label: "Sorry, I've got to be somewhere."

walked-past.text: You get in the car. In the mirror he's fetching the ball again.

once.text: He scores on Saturday, low, and he doesn't look up. He finds you first.

thursdays-again.text: {if arc.bag==1}You get the bag out of your boot and leave it on the hook in the kit room, where it used to hang.{/if} Next Thursday he's out there before you are.

stopped-short.text: He collects the balls on his own.

callbacks.line: He runs past the others to you and holds up ten fingers.
"I'm not taking it easy on you because of Thursdays."

event.title: A photo of the back of a hand
event.speaker: kitman
setup: A picture message from a number you don't have saved. It's the back of an old man's hand with "THURS - {kid.short}" written on it in biro.
"New kit man rang me. Is the lad any good? D"

choices.label: "Better than I was. Come and count for us."

outcomes.text: He comes the next Thursday with two flasks, and sits on a fold-up chair by the shed.

choices.label: "Not yet. He looks at the keeper."

ends.title: The bag moves on
ends.text: You stayed out with him, you went to his night, and the bag ended up on pitch two with another lad.

ends.title: The empty chair
ends.text: You told him you'd come and you didn't, and the chair with your name on it is in the photographs.

ends.title: You went in
ends.text: He offered, and you went in with the others.

arcs.title: The legend in the circle
arcs.summary: The club's record scorer turns up at training and plays you one against one in front of the squad, for his boots or your car. After that he is on the television for every big game you play. Two clocks race: play well and keep your word and he becomes your mentor; duck him or let him down and he becomes your critic. At 30 you are the one in the circle.
arcs.clockRule: The first clock to fill sets arc.path (mentor or critic) and stops the other.

event.title: The man by the cones
event.speaker: legend
setup: There's a man in a long coat by the cones, keeping a ball up in his ordinary shoes. The whole squad has stopped to watch him do it.
It's {legend.name}. He scored 213 for this club and his face is on the side of the main stand. {captain.short} says, quietly: "The gaffer's given him ten minutes. He asked which one was you."

say: He lets the ball drop and puts his foot on it. "They tell me you're the one. I'm fifty-one and I've a plastic hip on the left side, and I'd still fancy taking this off you. First to three?"

replies.label: "First to three."
"I don't want to be the one who breaks your hip."
"I've got a recovery session. Another day."
Say nothing.

say: A few of the lads laugh. "Son, I had centre-halves trying to break it for fifteen years, and the surgeon managed it in forty minutes. Get your boots on."

replies.label: "First to three, then."
"I mean it, not today."

say: Nobody speaks. He rolls the ball across the grass and it stops against your foot. "That's yours, then. I'll stand here."

replies.label: Put your foot on it.
Pass it back to him and walk to the gym.

say: {captain.short}, behind you, not quietly: "He's got a recovery session." Somebody does a chicken noise. {legend.short} is already picking his coat up.

replies.label: "Fine, put the coat down and we'll play to three."
Go to the gym.

say: "Good. Now, we play for something, or it's only exercise and I get plenty of that with the dog. What have you got?"

replies.label: "My boots against yours."
"My car against your boots."
"A handshake. I don't bet on football."

say: "I'm in my shoes. The boots I'd put up are in a glass box in my hall, the ones from the cup final, and my wife dusts them on a Sunday."
{if talk.mood>=1}"I'll tell you what. You've got a bit about you. Those against whatever you drove here in."{/if}{if talk.mood<1}"Those against yours, and I want yours signed."{/if}

replies.label: "The car it is, then."
"Boots for boots, and I'll sign mine."
"Let's keep it to a handshake."

say: He looks over at the car park. "Which one's yours? ... That'll do. My daughter's just passed her test." The lads are loving this.

replies.label: "She'll be walking a while yet. Shall we?"
"Actually, make it boots for boots."

say: The squad has made a ring about fifteen yards across.

"Here's how it goes. You get past me and stop the ball dead on the far side, that's one to you. I take it off you, that's one to me. Three goes each way if we need them. {captain.short}, you count, and don't be kind to me."

replies.label: "My ball first."
"You have it first, you're the guest."

activity.name: First to three
activity.intro: Get past him and stop the ball on the far side of the ring. He doesn't chase, he waits for you to make the first move.

dials.hisGoes: rolled from his rating and shown, as the crossbar team-mate's shots are

say: Three-nil. He sits down on the ball bag and gets his breath, and the lads have gone a bit quiet because nobody expected three-nil.
"Well. You didn't need to enjoy it that much."

replies.label: Offer him a hand up.
"Your daughter's still walking."

say: {activity.score}-{activity.oppScore}, to you. He bends over with his hands on his knees. "Thirty years ago you'd not have got one off me, and I'd have told you about it all the way to the car park."

replies.label: "You took {activity.oppScore} off me with a plastic hip."
"Good game, that. Are you all right?"

say: {if arc.wager=='none'}"A handshake, we said." He shakes your hand for longer than you expect.{/if}
{if arc.wager!='none'}"A bet's a bet. The boots'll be at the front desk tomorrow. They're a nine and a half and I had the left one stretched, so don't go wearing them."{/if}

replies.label: "I'll look after them."
"Keep them in the hall. Come and watch me instead."
"I'm wearing them Saturday."
Shake his hand.

say: Three-two to him, and he's blowing. "You went left every single time. Did you know that? Five goes, five times left. I only had to guess once."

replies.label: "I didn't know that, and fair enough, you won."
"Double or nothing."
"You fouled me on the last one."

say: Three-{activity.score}, to a man of fifty-one in his shoes. "You went left every time. I only had to stand there." {captain.short} is filming it.

replies.label: "You won. What do I owe you?"
"Double or nothing."
Walk off towards the gym.

say: You've stepped out of the ring with the game still going. {captain.short}: "That's a forfeit, that. Three-nil to the old man."

replies.label: Come back and settle up.

say: "Double what? I've already got your {arc.wager}." He thinks about it. "Go on, then. I win again and you clean my dog's kennel out, every Thursday for a month, and the lads can come and watch."

replies.label: "First to three."
"No, you won, so I'll pay."

say: "Right. That's us level, and I'm not playing a third because I'd like to walk tomorrow." He gives you your {arc.wager} back. "You went right twice. So you can learn."

replies.label: "I'll take level."

say: He wins it again. "Thursdays, eight o'clock, bottom pitch. Bring rubber gloves. He's a big dog."

replies.label: "Eight o'clock, and I'll bring the gloves."

say: {if arc.wager=='car'}He holds his hand out for the keys. The lads have stopped laughing, because he means it.{/if}
{if arc.wager=='boots'}"Boots. And sign them, to Margaret, she'll want to know whose they were."{/if}
{if arc.wager=='none'}"A handshake, we said." He shakes it. "Thursdays I walk the dog round the bottom pitch at eight, if you want to find out about your right side."{/if}

replies.label: Hand them over.
"It was a joke. You're not having my car."
"I'll be there Thursday with a ball."

say: He's putting his coat back on. "Two things before I go. I do the co-commentary on your cup games now, and I say what I see. I'm telling you to your face so you don't get it off your mum."
"And my grandson's team have their presentation night in May, the under-elevens. Somebody has to give out the medals and they're sick of me. Will you do it?"

replies.label: "Tell them I'll be there."
"May's a long way off. Ask me nearer the time."
"I don't do kids' parties."

ducked.text: From the gym window you can see him doing keep-ups with the under-18s. Nobody in the squad mentions it to you today.

ducked-cold.text: He traps it and watches you go. "Hm," he says, to nobody in particular.

welshed.text: "Was it?" He puts his hand back in his pocket. Twenty-odd team-mates watched you shake on it, and none of them is looking at you now.

won-promised.text: "Good. Second Friday in May, at the cricket club. I'll write it on something." The lads clap him all the way to his car.

promise.text: Give out the medals at {legend.short}'s grandson's presentation night

remind.line: "Friday. Cricket club. 6.30. They've made a banner. L"

won.text: "I'll ask you nearer the time, then." The lads clap him all the way to his car.

won-cold.text: "No. I don't suppose you do." He zips his coat up to the chin.

lost-promised.text: "Good lad. Second Friday in May." {if arc.wager=='car'}He drives your car out of the car park himself, slowly, with the window down.{/if}

promise.text: Give out the medals at {legend.short}'s grandson's presentation night

remind.line: "Friday. Cricket club. 6.30. They've made a banner. L"

lost.text: {if arc.wager=='car'}He drives your car out of the car park himself, slowly, with the window down. You get a lift home off {captain.short}.{/if}{if arc.wager!='car'}He goes, and the session starts twenty minutes late.{/if}

lost-cold.text: "Lost, and too busy for children. All right." {if arc.wager=='car'}He takes the keys off you without another word.{/if}

callbacks.line: "Still got that recovery session?"
"Go left, trust me, you always do."
{captain.short} still has the video on his phone and shows it to every new signing.
"You want me to shake on it, with you?"

event.title: "I'll say what I see"
event.speaker: legend
setup: The clip from the television gantry is all over your feed by the time you're on the coach.

{if lastRating>=7.8 && arc.result=='won'}{legend.name}: "He beat me in a ring of cones on a Tuesday, and I said then it was a Tuesday. Well, that was a cup tie and he's done it again. I'll stop mentioning Tuesdays."{/if}

{if lastRating>=7.8 && arc.result!='won'}{legend.name}: "I've been hard on this lad. I took his {if arc.wager=='car'}car{/if}{if arc.wager!='car'}pride{/if} off him at the training ground, and he's turned up tonight and played like that. I'd want him in my team."{/if}

{if lastRating<6.0 && arc.result=='won'}{legend.name}: "He beat a fifty-one-year-old with a plastic hip, and good luck to him. Tonight he had a fit centre-half and I didn't see him go past him once."{/if}
{if lastRating<6.0 && arc.result=='lost'}{legend.name}: "He goes left. I found that out in three minutes in my shoes, and tonight their full-back found it out as well."{/if}
{if lastRating<6.0 && arc.result=='ducked'}{legend.name}: "I went to their training ground to have a look at him and he had a recovery session. I thought about that a few times tonight."{/if}
{hack.name} of {hack.outlet} has tagged you: "Any reply?"

say: "{legend.short} has had his say. Do you want yours? I'll print it as you give it."

replies.label: "He's earned the right to say it."
"I'll answer him on the pitch."
"Tell him the ring of cones is always open."
"He retired before I was born. Next question."
No comment.

say: "Is that a challenge? Can I write that it's a challenge?"

replies.label: "Thursday, eight o'clock. He knows where."
"Write that I'm smiling."

took-it.text: {hack.short} prints it straight. {legend.short} likes the post, which his grandson must have shown him how to do.

silent.text: You don't reply, and by Monday it has gone away.

rematch-called.text: The headline is "THURSDAY, 8PM". There are about forty people at the bottom pitch fence that week, and one of them has brought a dog to meet his dog.

bit-back-on-air.text: It leads the back page. He's asked about it on the radio the next morning and says "He's right, I did," and nothing else, which is worse.

callbacks.line: "Still here. Still not born yesterday."

event.title: Thursdays, bottom pitch
event.speaker: legend

entry.hint: Thursdays at eight, with the dog

setup: Eight in the morning on the bottom pitch. {legend.name} is throwing a tennis ball for a very large, very slow dog.

say: {if mem(legend,'welshed-on-the-bet')}"I wondered when you'd turn up. Have you brought me a car?"{/if}
{if mem(legend,'you-ducked-him')}"No recovery session this morning, then."{/if}
{if arc.result=='lost' && !mem(legend,'welshed-on-the-bet')}"You came. I'll be honest, most of them don't. His name's Stanley, and he'll want your glove."{/if}
{if arc.result=='won' || arc.result=='level'}"The newspaper says you've called me out. Stanley's not impressed."{/if}

replies.label: Give him the keys. "A bet's a bet."
"Show me what I do wrong on my right side."
"First to three. Same ring."
"What was it like, the 213th?"
Throw the ball for the dog.

say: He looks at the keys for a long time. "I'd written this off. Our Kelly'll have it, she's been getting two buses." He puts them in his coat. "Right. Get a ball."

replies.label: Get a ball.

say: Stanley brings it back to you and not to him. "He's never done that. He bit the last manager."

replies.label: "Have you got ten minutes for my right side?"
Give the dog a pat and go in.

say: "Everybody asks about 213. Nobody asks about 212, and I was on 212 for eleven games. I couldn't sleep, I was horrible to live with, and I missed a penalty at home in the middle of it."
"The one that broke it went in off my shin from four yards. That's the goal on the side of the stand. They've painted it so it looks like I meant it."

replies.label: "Off your shin. I'm telling everyone."
"I won't tell anybody that."

say: "Go and stand over there. You're going to go past me on your right ten times, and each time I'm going to tell you what your shoulders did before your feet moved. They give you away, the shoulders."

replies.label: Go and stand over there.

activity.name: Right side only
activity.intro: Ten goes. Only a go that beats him on your right counts.
activity.score: times past him on the right (0-10)

say: "{activity.score} out of ten on the side you don't like. That's a different player to the one in the ring."

replies.label: "Same time next week?"

say: "{activity.score}. Your shoulders are still telling me. Come back, it took me a year and I was cleverer than you."

replies.label: "I'll come back."
"This is a waste of a morning."

say: "That's that settled, then." He's smiling, and he's rubbing his hip. "Stanley, we're going home. I've been beaten by a child."

replies.label: "Same time next week. I'll bring the coffees."
"Will you say that on the telly?"

say: "Three-{activity.score}. You went left twice. That's better than five times."

replies.label: "Can I come back next Thursday?"

dog-only.text: The dog watches you all the way to the changing rooms.

thursday-walk.text: {if arc.paid==1}He drives home in your old car. {/if}You can feel it in your hips for two days.

stormed.text: "It took me a year," he says again, to your back.

settled.text: The star pass stop closes. You bring the coffees. He has four sugars, and you're not to tell his wife.

settled-on-air.text: He does, on the Saturday, in front of two million people: "He beat me fair and square and I'd like it noted that I was fifty-one."

callbacks.line: "I see him on a Thursday morning. He's working on it, I'll say that."

event.title: The cricket club, second Friday in May
event.speaker: legend

entry.text: "Friday. Cricket club. 6.30. They've made a banner. L"

clash.line: It's two days before a match, and the gaffer likes you home early.

setup: A function room over a cricket pavilion, with sixty children in it and a banner that has your name spelt wrong.
{legend.short} gives you a carrier bag of medals. "There are forty-one of them. Every child gets one, and the goalkeeper gets two because he cried."

say: A boy of about ten with {legend.short}'s chin has walked straight up to you. "Grandad says you only go left. Is that true?"

replies.label: "It was. He's fixing it. Don't tell him it's working."
"Your grandad scored off his shin."
"Get in that goal and find out."

activity.name: Forty-one penalties
activity.intro: You are in goal on the outfield. The under-elevens take a penalty each. Let a few in.

say: You've saved seven penalties off ten-year-olds, and one of them is in tears. {legend.short} has his head in his hands. "What's the matter with you?"

replies.label: "Retakes. I wasn't ready for any of them."
"They've got to learn."

say: It takes an hour, because every child wants a photo and two of them want you to sign a cast. Afterwards he walks you down to the car park. "You said you'd come and you came. I've had internationals who didn't."

replies.label: "Same again next May, if they'll have me."
"I said I would."

kept-medals.text: The banner is in the back of his car. He says they'll fix the spelling for next year.

kept-medals-again.text: "I'll tell them tonight, they'll not sleep." {if said:saved-them-all}One father is still looking at you from across the car park.{/if}

promise.text: Do the medals again next May

@send-apologies.text: You send forty-one signed photos in a box. He hands them out himself. On the Saturday he's asked about you on air, and he says: "He's a busy lad."

@ignore.text: Sixty children and a banner, and nobody to give out the medals. He does it himself. On the Saturday, live: "He stood in a ring of cones and told me to my face he'd come. He didn't come."

callbacks.line: "I'll say he played well. I'll not say more than that about him."

event.title: A landline number
event.speaker: legend
setup: The night before a big one, and your phone shows a landline. He's the only person you know who rings from one.

say: "It's me. I'm not doing the commentary tomorrow. I've told them I can't be fair about you any more, so they've got somebody else, and I'll be in the stand with Margaret."

replies.label: "You've never been fair about me."
"That means a lot, coming from you."
Say nothing.

say: "I rang to tell you something, so let me tell you. The night before my final I was sick in the hotel sink, twice. I've never told a journalist that. I scored in the first ten minutes and I was fine after."
{if arc.boots==0}"The boots are at your front desk. Don't argue, Margaret's sick of dusting them. They're a nine and a half so don't wear them."{/if}

replies.label: "What do I do if it's not going in?"
"I'll aim for my shin."

say: "Go right. Once, early, even if you lose it. Then their full-back spends the rest of the afternoon wondering." You can hear the dog in the background. "Go to bed."

replies.label: "Goodnight. Say hello to Stanley."

blessed.text: At the ground the next day there's a seat in the directors' box with his coat on it, and he lifts one hand when you look up.

callbacks.line: He's in the directors' box. He taps his right shoulder.

event.title: "He's gone soft"
event.speaker: hack
setup: In the mixed zone {hack.name} holds his phone up so you can watch {legend.name} in the studio from twenty minutes ago.

"I've stopped making excuses for him. {if mem(legend,'never-came-to-the-medals')}He let sixty children down and never rang. {/if}{if mem(legend,'welshed-on-the-bet')}He shook my hand on a bet and never paid it. {/if}{if mem(legend,'you-ducked-him')}He wouldn't even play me. {/if}This club has had some proper number nines. He isn't one, and I'd sell him."

say: "He says he'd sell you. What do you say to {legend.short}?"

replies.label: "He's right about tonight. I was poor."
"He's entitled to his opinion."
"I'll go and see him. This isn't for you lot."
"He's a bitter old man with a microphone."
No comment.

say: "And the rest of it? The things he says you did?"

replies.label: "He's right about that as well. I'll put it right."
"That's between me and him."

cold-war.text: It runs for three days in the papers, and he carries on saying it on the radio for another month.

war.text: Back page, front page, and the phone-ins. Half the ground sings his name at you the next home game, and it is your own half.

go-and-see-him.text: Thursday, eight o'clock, the bottom pitch. He's there with the dog. He doesn't say hello, he just points at the ring of cones he's already put out.

callbacks.line: "My dad says you called {legend.short} bitter. My dad says you're not fit to lace his boots."

event.speaker: legend
setup: You're on 212 for the club, one short of him. A steward says there's somebody asking for you in the directors' box, and that he's brought his own flask.
{if arc.path=='critic'}You haven't spoken to him in years.{/if}

say: {if arc.path=='mentor'}"Sit down. I told you about 212, didn't I? How long have you been on it?"{/if}
{if arc.path!='mentor'}"Sit down, I'm not going to bite. I said some things on the television and I meant most of them at the time. How long have you been on 212?"{/if}

replies.label: "Four games. I'm not sleeping."
"It's a number. It'll come."
"Why do you care how long?"

say: "I was on it for eleven. I want you to get it, and I want to be here when you do. So I'm asking you: when it goes in, will you come over to this box? Margaret wants a photograph and I'd like to shake your hand in front of them all."

replies.label: "I'll come straight to you."
"I've got my own celebration planned."
"After what you said about me? No."

promised-the-box.text: He pours you a cup of tea out of the flask, and it has four sugars in it.

promise.text: When you score number 213, go to {legend.short}'s box

kept.text: You run the length of the stand and he's already halfway down the steps. The picture is on the side of the stand by the autumn, next to his.

broken.text: You slide on your knees in front of the away end. On the big screen they cut to his box, and he's standing up clapping with nobody to shake hands with.

own-way.text: "Aye, well. It's your goal." He screws the lid back on the flask.

refused.text: "That's fair." He's there anyway the day you score it, in his own seat, and he claps.

event.title: "The gaffer's given us ten minutes"
event.speaker: kid
setup: You're thirty-odd and you've come out early to do your stretches. The squad is already in a ring on pitch one, and {kid.name}, who is {kid.age}, is standing in the middle of it with a ball under his foot.
{if arc.path=='mentor'}On the touchline there's an old man in a long coat with a very old dog. He has brought a fold-up chair.{/if}

say: "The lads say you did this to {if legend}{legend.short}{/if}{if !legend}the old number nine{/if} when you were my age. {if arc.result=='won'}They say you won.{/if}{if arc.result=='lost'}They say he took your {arc.wager} off you.{/if}{if arc.result=='ducked'}Actually they say you didn't turn up.{/if}"
"So I'm asking. First to three?"

replies.label: "Give me a minute to warm my hamstrings up."
"Who put you up to this?"
"I've got a recovery session."
Say nothing.

say: {captain.short}: "Nobody put him up to it. He asked me last week if he was allowed." The kid has gone red.

replies.label: "You're allowed. First to three."
"Not today, son."

say: "Oh. Okay." He picks the ball up. {if mem(squad,'saw-you-duck-the-legend')}Somebody at the back does the chicken noise, and it's a man who was here the first time.{/if}

replies.label: "Put it down. Go on, first to three."
Go and do your stretches.

say: "What are we playing for? {captain.short} said there has to be something."

replies.label: "My boots against yours."
"A pair of cup final boots, nine and a half."
"You win, you can have my car."
"You lose, you give the medals out in May."

activity.name: First to three
activity.intro: He is quicker than you and he knows it. You've done this before and he hasn't.

dials.hisGoes: rolled from his pace against your age and reading, and shown

say: {activity.score}-{activity.oppScore} to you. He's sat on the grass. "I went for the ball every time and it wasn't there."

replies.label: "You dive in. Thursday, eight, bottom pitch."
"You went left. Every time. Somebody told me that once."
"Come back when you've got 200 goals."

say: Three-{activity.score} to him. You've got your hands on your knees. He doesn't know whether he's allowed to celebrate.

replies.label: Pay up. "Thirty years from now, you do the same."
Hold your hand out so he can pull you up.
"My hamstring went."

you-ducked.text: The ring breaks up. {if arc.path=='mentor'}The old man folds his chair and doesn't wave.{/if}

you-won-mentor.text: He's there on Thursday before you are. {if arc.path=='mentor'}So is the old man, with two flasks, and it turns out he has opinions on the kid's shoulders as well.{/if}

you-won-hard.text: The lads laugh and he stays sat on the grass. He'll have 200 goals one day, and he'll remember who said that to him.

you-lost-paid.text: {if arc.wager2=='legend-boots'}You give him the cup final boots, and tell him they're a nine and a half and he's not to wear them. {/if}{if arc.wager2=='car'}You give him the keys. He's seventeen and hasn't got a licence, so his mum drives it home. {/if}The video is everywhere by lunchtime, and you find you don't mind.

you-lost-sulked.text: Nobody says anything. The physio checks the hamstring that afternoon and writes "fine" on the form.

callbacks.line: He finds you in the stand and holds up one finger. One down.
He's wearing your old boots in training. They're half a size too big for him.

ends.title: The circle carries on
ends.text: You played the old number nine in the ring at eighteen, and at thirty a kid played you.

ends.title: A recovery session
ends.text: You were asked to play in the ring at eighteen and again at thirty, and both times you went to the gym.

arcs.title: The man who did your ankle
arcs.summary: Nobody writes this rival in advance. An ordinary opponent puts you out for weeks with a tackle and the game promotes him to a person: a name you know, two traits, a title, a record of every meeting. Each time he gets the better of you he goes up in the world, and each time you beat him he comes back having learned something. The feud ends with a handshake, with a shared dressing room, or it never ends.

generator.promotedFrom: an opposition player who is INVENTED (a club with no real squad, a generated youth player, or an invented signing). Never a real footballer: the game would be writing insults for a real person.

record.scar: one thing that stays visible, from the list

styles.name: Talker
styles.inMatch: a line from him at the walkout and after every chance you miss
styles.line: "How's the ankle? I've been thinking about it."

styles.name: Golden boy

styles.line: "No hard feelings. I've never had any, about anybody."

styles.name: Grafter

weaknesses.name: Slow on the turn

weaknesses.how: he always honours a wager, and expects you to

scars.text: You play with that ankle strapped for the rest of the season, and it shows on your player.
The clip of you putting it through his legs is pinned to the top of his replies for a year.
He has a three-match ban on his record with your name on the referee's report.
He has a scar through his left eyebrow from the clash, and he touches it when he sees you.

promotion.when: he wins a meeting (his side win and you do not score, or he is rated higher)
do: the next transfer window he moves to a club one step bigger, or gets the armband
title is rebuilt from the scoreline: 'Two-nil {nem.short}'
he comes back changed: add the trait 'has done his homework' (your favourite side is covered) or swap his weakness
he is in the squad when you get an international call-up, or he is across the tunnel when you get one for another nation

match: walkout line by trait and last meeting
he celebrates in front of you if he scores
the commentary names the history once per match
press: the tabloid man asks about him before every meeting
he is quoted about you when you are injured, dropped or transferred
transfers: his new club appears in your summer list with a line under it: '{nem.short} plays here'
his club may bid for you; signing makes him a team-mate and opens the dressing-room beat
people: he has a card on the People page with his title, traits, scar and the meetings row by row

example.note: One worked nemesis, as the generator would fill it, so the lines below can be read with real words in them.

nem.name: Callum Brandt
nem.title: the man who did your ankle

event.title: "I got the ball"
event.speaker: nem
setup: You're on the bed in the away physio room with your boot cut off and ice strapped round the ankle. {physio.short} has said "weeks" and won't say how many.
There's a knock, and {nem.name} of {nem.club} is in the doorway, still in his kit. He's the one who went through you.

say: "I came to see how it was. I got the ball, for what it's worth. I've watched it back on the kit man's phone and I got the ball first."

replies.label: "It's a contact sport. Thanks for coming in."
"You got the ball and then you got me."
"Get out. You knew what you were doing."
Say nothing.

say: He stands there a bit longer than is comfortable. "Right. Well, I came." He puts something on the end of the bed. It's the shirt he played in, and he's signed it.

replies.label: Nod at him.
Push it onto the floor with your good foot.

say: {physio.short} has stepped between you. {nem.short}, over his shoulder: "I came in here to be decent. I'll not bother next time."

replies.label: "There won't be a next time. I'll see you first."
"...Wait. Sit down a minute."

say: "The gaffer told us to let you know we were there in the first ten minutes. That's all he said. I did my cruciate two years ago and I was out for nine months, so I'm not somebody who goes looking to do that to people."
"How long have they said?"

replies.label: "Weeks. He won't say how many."
"I'll be back before you play us again."
"Your gaffer told you to do that?"

say: {if said:asked-about-gaffer}"I didn't say that, and if you tell the papers I said that, I'll say you were on painkillers."{/if}
"We play you at ours in the spring. If you're fit and you score past us, I'll send you this shirt, washed, with whatever you want written on it, and if you don't, you send me yours."

replies.label: "Done, so get a pen ready."
"No bet, but thanks for coming in."
"The shirt, and you say sorry on camera."

decent.text: He nods and goes. {physio.short} says, "That's more than most of them do," and puts more ice on it.

shook-on-it.text: He shakes your hand, carefully, because of the drip. The shirt stays on the end of the bed.

debt.text: A signed shirt rides on the spring fixture at {nem.club}

raised.text: "On camera." He thinks. "And if you don't score, you say on camera that it was a fair tackle." You shake on that.

debt.text: A shirt and a sentence on camera ride on the spring fixture at {nem.club}

threw-his-shirt.text: He picks it up off the floor himself and folds it. "All right," he says, and he goes. {physio.short} doesn't say anything.

threatened.text: He laughs once and goes. A steward was in the corridor, and it's in the tabloids by Tuesday: "I'LL SEE YOU FIRST".

callbacks.line: {nem.short} is across the tunnel. He looks at your ankle before he looks at your face.
"I've still got that shirt. It's been on a floor, mind."

event.title: "It's a man's game"
event.speaker: hack
setup: You're on the sofa with your foot up on two cushions. {nem.short} scored at the weekend, and {hack.name} asked him about you afterwards.
{if arc.sorry==1}The quote in {hack.outlet}: "I went to see him. He's a good lad and I hope he's back soon. It was a fair challenge."{/if}
{if arc.sorry==0}The quote in {hack.outlet}: "I went to see him and got told where to go. It's a man's game. Maybe he should try another one."{/if}
Then a text from {hack.short}: "Your turn. One line?"

say: "I've a space on the back page. What do you want in it?"

replies.label: "He came to see me. That's the end of it."
"I'm working on getting fit. Ask me in the spring."
"Tell him I'll bring a pen for the shirt."
"He's a clogger and his gaffer sent him to do it."
No comment.

say: You leave {hack.short} on read. An hour later there's a text from a number you don't have.
{if arc.sorry==1}"It's {nem.short}. Got your number off your physio, hope that's all right. How's the swelling? Mine took three weeks to go down."{/if}
{if arc.sorry==0}"It's {nem.short}. I meant what I said in the paper. But I didn't mean to do your ankle, and I can't sleep, so I'm telling you."{/if}

replies.label: "Down a bit. Thanks for asking."
"Sleep fine. I'll be the one keeping you up in spring."
Block the number.

cooled.text: {hack.short} is disappointed and prints it small, on page 60.

spring.text: "ASK ME IN THE SPRING" is the headline. The date of the fixture is printed under it.

public-bet.text: The bet is public now. A bookmaker puts odds on you scoring at {nem.club}, and somebody at the training ground has a tenner on it.

clogger.text: His club put out a statement. Yours fines you a week's wages, and {manager.short} makes you read the statement out in his office.

texting.text: He sends you his own rehab sheet from the cruciate, photographed page by page, and some of it's useful.

texting-edge.text: He sends back a laughing face and a picture of the shirt on a hanger.

blocked.text: He tells {hack.short} you blocked him. It makes a paragraph.

callbacks.line: "Clogger. My mum cut that one out."

event.title: Across the tunnel
event.speaker: nem
setup: The tunnel at {nem.club}. The two teams are lined up side by side, and he has swapped places with their left back so he's standing next to you.
{if nem.scar=='your-strapping'}Your ankle is strapped under the sock, and he has seen it.{/if}

say: {if arc.meetings==0 && arc.sorry==1}"You're back, then. I've got the shirt in my bag and there's a pen with it. How's the ankle?"{/if}
{if arc.meetings==0 && arc.sorry==0}"I heard you were looking for me. Well, I'm here, I'm number five."{/if}
{if arc.meetings>=1 && arc.heWon>arc.youWon}"That's {arc.heWon} to me and {arc.youWon} to you. I've stopped bringing the pen."{/if}
{if arc.meetings>=1 && arc.youWon>=arc.heWon}"I've watched every one of your goals since last time. You open your body up before you shoot. I'm telling you now so it's fair."{/if}

replies.label: "The ankle's fine, and have a good game."
"Which side do you want me to go past you?"
"Who gets the first tackle in, you or me?"
Look straight ahead.

say: {if said:threat}"Careful. The ref's standing right behind you." He is.{/if}
{if arc.wager=='none'}"Loser buys the other one a drink in the players' lounge. That's all. I'm not a gambler."{/if}
{if arc.wager!='none'}"Same bet as the physio room. You score, you get the shirt{if arc.wager=='apology'} and I say it on camera{/if}. You don't, I get yours."{/if}

replies.label: "You're on."
"And the loser carries the winner's boots off."
"I'm here to win a football match."

activity.name: You against {nem.short}
activity.intro: The real match. The duel is scored from it: your goals, your dribbles past him, his tackles on you, cards.
activity.score: duel points: your goal +2, dribble past him +1, his clean tackle on you +1 to him, his side win and you blank +2 to him
needs: mode:match-duel (a tracker over the real match; no new football)

say: Full time. He comes to find you in the centre circle with the shirt already in his hand. "What do you want written on it?"

replies.label: "Just your name, and come for that drink."
"'I got the ball.' And sign it."
"Keep it, I don't want it in my house."

say: Full time, and you didn't get a kick. He's waiting by the tunnel with his hand out, and it's for the shirt off your back.

replies.label: Take it off and give it to him.
"I'll send it. I'm not doing it out here."
Walk past him down the tunnel.

say: Honours even. "Nobody's getting a shirt off that. Same again next time?"

replies.label: "Same again."
"Come and have that drink anyway."

say: He was sent off on the hour for the second one on you. He's waiting outside your dressing room in his suit, with his bag over his shoulder.

replies.label: "Go on, what did you want to say?"
Go in and shut the door.

you-won-gracious.text: He has a lemonade because he's driving. You find out he has a daughter who's three and supports your club, which he says he's working on.

you-won-funny.text: He writes it, and he underlines "ball" twice. It goes on the wall at home and every team-mate who comes round reads it out.

you-won-cruel.text: He stands there holding it. There's a camera on the two of you, and that's the picture the papers use.

he-won-paid.text: You walk off in your undershirt in front of their end. He holds your shirt up to them, and then he folds it properly.{if arc.raise==1} You carry his boots in as well, as agreed.{/if}

he-won-owed.text: "Two weeks," he says. "I'll be checking the post."

settle.text: You sign it and post it. He sends a photo of it framed, in his downstairs toilet.

ifUnpaid.text: He posts a picture of an empty coat hanger with your name under it. It gets 40,000 likes.

he-won-welshed.text: "That's twice you've walked past me," he shouts down the tunnel. Both dressing rooms hear it.

level.text: He nods and jogs off to his own end.

level-drink.text: The players' lounge at {nem.club} is a portable cabin with a tea urn. He gets them in.

red-talk.text: "I lost my head, and I shouldn't have. I'll get three games for it." He goes before you can say anything back. The ban goes on his record with your name in the referee's report.

red-door.text: He's still out there when the coach leaves. He comes back from the ban a different player: he doesn't dive in on you again, and he's harder to beat for it.

callbacks.line: "Your shirt's in my downstairs toilet, by the way. Framed."
He's put a strip of tape on his left wrist with your number written on it.
"Have you posted that shirt yet?"

beats.title: He's gone up in the world

event.title: "Here We Go"
event.speaker: agent
setup: The agent rings while you're driving. "Have you seen it? {nem.name} has signed for {nem.newClub}. Four years, and they've given him the armband."
"I'm ringing because they asked about you first, in January, and went for him when your club said no. I thought you should hear that from me."

say: "They still want a forward. If I ring them back, you'd be in the same dressing room as him by August. Do I ring them?"

replies.label: "Ring them, I want to hear the number."
"I'm not sharing a dressing room with him."
"What does he say about it?"
Say nothing. Keep driving.

say: {if nem.grudge>=40}"He was asked in his first press conference. He said, 'I'd play with anybody. I'd also tackle anybody in training.' Make of that what you like."{/if}
{if nem.grudge<40}"He was asked in his first press conference. He said you're the best he's played against and he'd sooner you were on his side. He's told them to go back in for you."{/if}

replies.label: "Ring them."
"I'm happy where I am. Tell them thanks."

say: "I'll ring them tonight. One thing. If this goes through, the first day of pre-season is you and him in a room together. Have you thought about what you say to him?"

replies.label: "I shake his hand and we start again."
"I tell him the armband doesn't mean he tells me."
"I've no idea, so get me the number first."

never.text: "Understood. I'll tell them no." It's in {hack.outlet} by Friday that you turned them down because of him, and neither of you told them.

left-it.text: "I'll take that as a not yet." He hangs up. {nem.newClub} are on your list in the summer window, and under their name it says who plays there.

stayed.text: "Good. Your club will like hearing that." He makes sure they do.

interest.text: {nem.newClub} go to the top of your list for the summer window, marked Very keen. Under their name it says: {nem.short} plays here.

callbacks.line: "Plenty of room in our dressing room. I measured it for you."

event.title: The peg next to his
event.speaker: nem
setup: First day at {you.club}. The kit man has put you on the peg next to {nem.name}, and you can't tell if he knew.
{nem.short} is already changed. Everyone in the room has found a reason to tie their laces slowly.

say: "Before anybody else says it. I did your ankle{if mem(nem,'took-your-shirt')}, I've got your shirt in my toilet{/if}{if mem(nem,'you-scored-past-him')}, you scored past me and made me sign for it{/if}. Is there anything on your side you want out in front of this lot?"

replies.label: Hold your hand out. "Same team now."
"Only that the armband doesn't make you my boss."
"Yes. Stay away from my ankles in training."
Hang your coat up and say nothing.

say: {if talk.mood>=1}Somebody laughs and the room breathes out. "I'll stay off your ankles. I'm on the other end of your crosses now, so you can pay me back that way."{/if}
{if talk.mood<1 && talk.mood>-2}"Fine. It doesn't. But I pick who takes the penalties, and at the minute that's me."{/if}
{if talk.mood<=-2}"Suit yourself." He picks up his boots. "Five-a-side in ten minutes. I've put us on opposite teams."{/if}

replies.label: "Then we settle the penalties now. Five each."
"Keep the penalties. I'll take the goals."

activity.name: Five each for the penalties
activity.intro: Five penalties each at the first-team keeper, in front of the squad. The better score takes them this season.

dials.hisGoes: rolled from his penalty rating and shown

say: {activity.score}-{activity.oppScore}. "They're yours. I'll tell the gaffer myself, so he doesn't think you went behind me."

replies.label: "Thanks, skipper."
"Told you."

say: {activity.oppScore}-{activity.score} to him. "I've taken them since I was sixteen. Ask me again at Christmas."

replies.label: "Christmas."

truce.text: The room goes back to its own business. By October he's the first one over when you score.

nemesis.title: the man who did your ankle, now your captain

pens-yours.text: He does tell the gaffer himself. You're on penalties, and he's the first one to you when the first one goes in.

pens-yours-edge.text: You're on penalties. He passes you the ball for the first one a bit harder than he needs to.

pens-his.text: He keeps them. At Christmas he comes and finds you, with a ball under his arm.

callbacks.line: {nem.short} gets to you first, all the way from centre-half.

event.title: Two men, one advert
event.speaker: nem

entry.text: "We've signed {nem.short} as well. We want the two of you in a cage for the advert. One day. Good money."

setup: A five-a-side cage under a railway arch, with lights and a film crew and a man holding a smoke machine. The director wants "real needle" between you.

{nem.short} is sat on an upturned crate with a paper cup, waiting for them to finish lighting it. {if nem.scar=='his-stitches'}He touches the scar in his eyebrow when he sees you, and then he laughs at himself for doing it.{/if}

say: "They want us to square up for the camera. I told them we've played each other {arc.meetings} times and you've never once squared up, you just go quiet. Was I right?"

replies.label: "You were right, I go quiet."
"Put the cup down and find out."
"Why did you say yes to this?"

say: "My daughter thinks you're brilliant. She's six now. She's got your poster up and I have to walk past it to get to the bathroom. I said yes so I could tell her I know you."

replies.label: "What's her name? I'll sign something."
"Past my poster. Every night."

say: "The director says first to three, you with the ball, and they'll film whatever happens. I say we make it worth something."
"If I stop you, you do a day at my lad's club's summer school. If you get three, I'll say on this advert, with the camera on, that I never got the ball."

replies.label: "On camera? Then let's go."
"I'll do the summer school either way."

dials.hisGoes: none: you attack every time, he defends

say: He's on the floor of the cage laughing, and the director shouts "Keep rolling."
He looks into the lens. "For the record, I got about a third of the ball and all of his ankle, and I've felt bad about it for {arc.years} years."

replies.label: Pull him up. "Took you long enough."
"Don't put that in the advert."

say: He's taken it off you three times and the crew are clapping him. "Summer school's the last week of July. Bring cones, they've never got enough cones."

replies.label: "Last week of July. I'll bring the cones."
"That was for the cameras. I'm not coming."

buried.text: They use it. It's the last five seconds of the advert, and it's the bit everyone shares.

nemesis.title: the man who never got the ball

buried-private.text: The director is furious and cuts it. {nem.short} texts you that night: "Thanks. My mum would have rung me."

summer-school.text: You shake on it with the camera still running.

promise.text: A day at {nem.short}'s lad's summer school, last week of July

kept.text: Ninety kids and eleven cones, until you open your boot. His lad nutmegs you and {nem.short} films it.

broken.text: The last week of July goes by. He says nothing in public. At the next meeting he doesn't look at you in the tunnel.

backed-out.text: The crew go quiet. "Right," he says. He finishes the day, does every shot they ask for, and doesn't speak to you again.

@ignore.text: They film it with him and an actor. The actor is taller than you.

callbacks.line: "A third of the ball," he says, and winks.

event.title: Both managers in the referee's room
event.speaker: manager
setup: It went off at full time. You and {nem.short} had hold of each other's shirts by the dugouts and it took four stewards.
Now you're sat outside the referee's room like two boys outside the head's office, with {manager.name} standing over you both.

say: "The referee's writing his report. He's asked me whether it's finished or whether he needs to put it all in. So is it finished?"

replies.label: "It's finished." Hold your hand out to him.
"Ask him. He started it {arc.years} years ago."
Say nothing.

say: {nem.short} speaks first. "It's finished on my side. I'm thirty next year and I'm tired of it." He holds his hand out, and everybody waits for you.

replies.label: Shake it.
Leave it there.

say: {if nem.grudge>=60}He looks at your hand. "No. You {if mem(nem,'kicked-his-shirt-on-the-floor')}put my shirt on a floor{/if}{if mem(nem,'never-sent-the-shirt')}never sent the shirt{/if}{if mem(nem,'called-him-a-clogger')}called me a clogger in the paper{/if}. Say sorry for that, and then I'll shake it."{/if}
{if nem.grudge<60}He takes it. "Finished."{/if}

replies.label: "I'm sorry for that. I was wrong."
"I'm not apologising to you."
"Finished."

shook.text: The referee leaves it out of the report. Two managers and four stewards saw the handshake, so it's in the papers anyway, with a different headline to the one they'd written.

never-shook.text: The referee puts it all in. You get two matches and he gets two. You never do shake his hand, and the papers bring that up before every game you play against him.

banned.text: The referee heard that through the door. Three matches for you and two for him, and {manager.short} doesn't speak to you on the coach.

callbacks.line: The cameras stay on the two of you at the handshakes. He walks past with his hand at his side.

event.title: His last game
event.speaker: nem
setup: A number you {if arc.path=='feud'}deleted years ago{/if}{if arc.path!='feud'}know{/if}. It's {nem.name}.
"I'm packing in at the end of the season. The knee's had enough of me. They're giving me a game, my eleven against a {nem.club} eleven, for the children's hospice."

say: {if arc.path=='feud'}"I know we never sorted it. That's why I'm ringing you and not getting somebody else to. I want you in my eleven. Up front. I've spent my whole career trying to stop you and I'd like to see what it's like when you're on my side."{/if}
{if arc.path!='feud'}"I want you up front in my eleven. I've done the numbers. You scored {arc.youWon} times in games against me, and I'd like some of that going the other way for once."{/if}

replies.label: "Tell me the date and I'll be there."
"Why would I do that for you?"
"Send me the date and I'll see."
Say nothing.

say: "Because I was twenty-four and my gaffer said let him know you're there, and I've thought about your ankle more than most of my goals."
"I've not got many goals, mind, I'm a centre-half. But I'd like one more go at getting it right."

replies.label: "All right, send me the date."
"Good luck with it, but I won't be there."

say: "Last Sunday in May, three o'clock. One condition. First tackle of the match is mine, on you, in training bibs, in the warm-up. I go in, I get all of the ball, and the photographer gets it. I want that picture for the wall."

replies.label: "All of the ball, and I'm holding you to that."
"What if it's the other way round and I tackle you?"

promised.text: It goes in your phone under Promises. His text arrives a minute later: the date, the postcode, and "bring shin pads".

promise.text: Play up front in {nem.short}'s last game, last Sunday in May

broken.text: He plays the game with ten and leaves your shirt on the bench, folded. That's the picture the papers use.

promised-swap.text: "Fine. But you've never made a tackle in your life, so I'll show you how first." It goes in your phone under Promises.

promise.text: Play up front in {nem.short}'s last game, last Sunday in May

see.text: He sends it. It sits in your messages with the two blue ticks on it.

refused.text: "Fair enough. I had to ask." He plays the game without you. A reporter asks him afterwards who the best he ever faced was, and he says your name and nothing more.

event.title: Last Sunday in May
event.speaker: nem
setup: Six thousand people at {nem.club} on a Sunday. In the warm-up he jogs over in a bib with a photographer behind him.
{if arc.swap==1}"Right. Stay on your feet, eyes on the ball, and don't lunge. Go on."{/if}{if arc.swap!=1}"Stand still. I've been practising."{/if}

activity.name: {nem.short}'s XI v {nem.club}
activity.intro: Twenty minutes, real match, you up front with him behind you at centre-half. He plays every long ball to you.
activity.score: your goals; an assist from him counts double
needs: mode:testimonial-match (the real match through EnginePlay with invited squads)

say: You've scored from his pass. He's run sixty yards to get to you, which takes him a while now. "I've watched you do that to me for years and I've never once enjoyed it till now."

replies.label: Take your shirt off and give it to him.
"Assist: the man who did my ankle."

say: Full time, and you haven't scored. "All those years I couldn't stop you, and the one day I want you to score, you don't. That's about right for me."

replies.label: Give him your shirt anyway.
"Get in goal. I'm not leaving without one."

gave-shirt.text: He puts it on over his own and wears both for the lap of the pitch. {if mem(nem,'took-your-shirt')}That makes two of yours he's got. He says this one's going in the living room.{/if}

laughed.text: Six thousand people laugh, and so does he. The hospice gets the gate money and the picture from the warm-up goes on his wall.

@ignore.text: He plays the game with ten and leaves your shirt on the bench, folded.

callbacks.line: {nem.short} has already asked if he can play centre-half in yours.
His name is on the list of people who said no.

ends.title: Old enemies
ends.text: He did your ankle when he was twenty-four, and years later you played up front in his last game.

ends.title: Team-mates
ends.text: You signed for his club and got the peg next to his.

ends.title: Team-mates, just about
ends.text: Same club, same dressing room, and he still passes it to you too hard.

ends.title: Never shook hands
ends.text: It started with a tackle, and the two of you never did shake hands.
